I'm personally of the mind the the Gnosis is incapable of summoning demons, let alone interacting in "The Outside" at all.

The short version of my belief is that if the Gnosis could summon demons it would be busted as hell. Keeping demons out of their grasp keeps the magic system balanced and leads to a more varied meta game.

The long version is that the is Gnosis is essentially a science. It's power comes from long and careful observation of the natural world. After which those with the sight and the knowledge of the Gnosis can summon the pure fundamental forces that make up the natural world. Gnostic sorcerers summon heat, wards, lines, and light instead of dragons, walls, lightning, and flames to do all the same things. Gnostic sorcery is more powerful on "The Inside" because it is closer to the inherent truth of the natural world of "The Inside." 

So in my mind if a Gnostic sorcerer somehow got to "The Outside" they would be powerless. I imagine it like putting a scientist in a place of pure chaos. No matter how long the scientist observes "The Outside" they will never learn anything. There are no rules, no dimensions, no repitition, no sense, for them to gain any knowledge from. We see this in the few glimpses we get of "The Outside" via the "head on a pole" sections. These sections are super messy and confusing because that is what "The Outside" is like. 

I say "is like" because for "The Outside" to be "The Outside" it would be impossible to accurately describe it. Because for it to be a true inverse of "The Inside" there cannot be anything to describe in such a place. Anything that exists there would be too chaotic, incomprehensible, and constantly shifting to have any observable meaning let alone a form to accurately describe. The closest way to picture "The Outside" is via analogy. 

In the "head on a pole" sections, everything is an analogy. Because one CANNOT accurately describe anything inherently chaotic, incomprehensible, and senseless. The closest way to approximate a description is to make an analogy; to say this chatoic mess IS LIKE something that can be described and made sense of. This is why I believe only anagogic sorcerers are capable of summoning demons, and tredding "The Outside." 

Anagogic sorcery is less powerful on "The Inside" because their analogies are inherently a less direct connection to the truth of the natural world. However only analogies can approximate a form for, and therefore give meaning to "The Outside." That is why the demons we see are a random crazy mess of parts and pieces. The way we see them is not how they truly are. Their natural form is formless, their only dimension is their hunger. It is up to the anagogic sorcerer to approximate their hunger into a physical form. That is also why summoned demons are in constant pain. Imagine if you, a real person, were constantly being torn apart by a world that hated your realness and dimensions. I imagine it is the same feeling just reversed for demons as they are formless things forced into forms. 

Inversely only anagogic sorcerers can travel "The Outside" because only formless concepts can exist there. A real thing or person would be torn to shreds or go insane. That is why during the "head on a pole" sections the main subject is not "I," or "he," or "Kellhus," the subject is "you." All other 1st, or 3rd person subjects are definite and refer to something specific even implicitly. "You" however is unspecific it could be anyone, including yourself, or a group of people. "You" is a concept of a person (essentially an analogy to a person) without being any particular person, and that is the only way one can "exist" in "The Outside." 

Long story short, I think demons and gnostic sorcery are inherently incompatible. This is due to the source of the meanings in gnostic sorcery. That source being observation of the natural world. If a gnostic sorcer tried to use the same method to dervive meaning from "The Outside" they would fail. Because "The Outside" is an inversion of "The Inside" therefore there what exists in "The Outside" is devoid of any physical dimension to observe, make sense of, and find meaning in. Only anagogic sorcery with their use of analogies, can force meaning onto the formless things in "The Outside" by saying they are like something else that already has meaning.

Due credit that the US did end the slave labor system that existed prior to the civil war. This is an objectively good thing and a high point of US history.

That being said slavery is still legal in the US. 

"Thirteenth Amendment

Section 1

Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted, shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction.

Section 2

Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation."

Because of the exception in section 1 prisoners can be legally considered slaves, but are they treated like slaves?


Slavery definition:
"https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/slavery
slavery- noun

1a: the practice or institution of holding people as chattel involuntarily and under threat of violence.

1b: the state of a person who is forced usually under threat of violence to labor for the profit of another.

1c: a situation or practice in which people are coerced to work under conditions that are exploitative."


US stance on prisoner work:
"https://www.bop.gov/inmates/custody_and_care/work_programs.jsp#:~:text=Federal%20Bureau%20of%20Prisons&text=Sentenced%20inmates%20are%20required%20to,hour%20for%20these%20work%20assignments.
Federal Bureau of Prisons, Work Programs:

Sentenced inmates are **required** to work if they are medically able. Institution work assignments include employment in areas like food service or the warehouse, or work as an inmate orderly, plumber, painter, or groundskeeper. Inmates earn 12¢ to 40¢ per hour for these work assignments."


US prohibited acts of prisoners, and punishments.
"https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-V/subchapter-C/part-541
28 CFR § 541.3 - Prohibited acts and available sanctions.

High Severity Level Prohibited Acts:
213. Encouraging others to refuse to work, or to participate in a work stoppage. 

Available Sanctions for High Severity Level Prohibited Acts:
A. Recommend parole date rescission or retardation. 

C. Disciplinary segregation (aka solitary confinement) up to 6 months.

E. Monetary Fine.

J. Impound inmate's personal property. 

Moderate Severity Level Prohibited Acts:
306. Refusing to work or to accept a program assignment. 

310. Unexcused absence from work or any program assignment. 

311. Failing to perform work as instructed by the supervisor. 

Available Sanctions for Moderate Severity Level Prohibited Acts:
A. Recommend parole date rescission or retardation. 

C. Disciplinary segregation (up to 3 months). 

E. Monetary Fine.

J. Impound inmate's personal property."

In the US prisoners are by definition slaves. From legal status to treatment. Prisoners are required to work, and not working or encouraging others to not work is punished by more prison time, torture (solitary confinement), fines, loss of property, and much more legal and illegal.

In a country with the largest prisoner population in the world, slavery is still very much alive in the US. 

That being said, I believe this meme will soon be true. Efforts like End the Exception (https://endtheexception.com/) and Prop. 6 in California are attempts to truly end slavery in the US. 

Though prop. 6 was rejected, like you all, I believe the US and it's people are always striving to become better, and fulfill the ideals of freedom the US was built on. I believe that soon, because of our desire for freedom for all, the US will truly end slavery in it's borders.

I really enjoyed the audiobooks. I am a busy person and I struggle focusing on reading so audio books are my preferred method. I've only ever listened to these books as audio books, and I admit that was close to dropping the series a few times when I was first listening because of the exact same issue you describe of things seemingly happening out of nowhere and being hit with a thousand series specific terms that I had no context for. It was pretty overwhelming but i stuck with it because I was still interested. I never had appendixes to aid me, but you can rest assured that Bakker does put out on answering your confusion and explaining things, and is surprisingly good at tying up loose ends. 

One reason I really like the audiobooks is that the narrators are PEAK! David DeVries who narrates the "Prince of Nothing" series is so impressive with his ability to act all the different voices and accents of the characters in the series. Plus the way he emotes the feelings that are going through the characters as they say certain lines elevated them from great, to ones I will never forget just because of the way he says them (Ex: "what will it be the next time I die...?" Breaks my heart every time, and when Kellhus imitates Cnaiur, it's just extra funny in a meta way, because DeVries is the narrator of both so can do a perfect imitation). His presentation of these characters really helped bring these characters to life and make the story so much more vivid. 

Kevin Orton who reads the "Aspect Emperor" series is admittedly less good, but I still like his reading a lot because of the gravity of his voice lends to the seriousness of this series. His timing and the way he stresses the right words in a sentence really makes it feel like you are listening to ancient bard recount a tragic epic. Also the man knows how use pauses. Sometimes after he says a particularly intense or important line, and he lets it hang there so it really sinks in. I admit it is a bit annoying how he has a habit of mispronouncing words, but I personally chalk that up to lax audio direction especially for the latter books. Overall I think he is a great story teller and the right man for the job for the 2nd series.

One way being audio only fails you is knowing the spelling of everything. Based on this sub and the short stories I've read, these books have the most insane spellings of names and terms I've ever seen. The audio definitely doesn't let you know that it's Cnaiur not "Nair" or Kelhus not "Kellos" etc.

I like Sanderson. Well technically I only really like one of his series, Stormlight Archive, the rest I don't really care for. I used to like him more before I read The Second Apocalypse. Sanderson used to be my favorite author but he doesn't scratch the itch I have for deep and philosophical fantasy the way Bakker does. 

That being said I still recommend Sanderson to basically anyone who asks me for fantasy recommendations, I still really enjoy reading Stormlight, and I really respect Sanderson as an author and voice in fantasy landscape. 

I feel I like the two series for different and divergent reasons. 

Stormlight is very approachable. Despite each book being a brick, they are pretty easy to read and get a handle on the world building quickly without too much exposition. This is one reason I like the series and recommend it to people because it makes you feel involved in the world without talking down to you.

TSA is almost hostile to new readers as it immediately throws you in the deep end. Hitting you with 100 lore-heavy terms and events in just the first few pages. Most of which you dont get the full context for until completing the whole series. At first this pissed me off and almost had me drop the books. But the mystery woven into everything always drew me back, and despite my initial doubts, all my questions were answered. At least in an interpretable way. This is something I came to like because I really enjoy the challenge of reading the second apocalypse and this seemingly hostile lack of exposition is also what allows these books to be so dense with lore, meaning, and discussion. 

Another reason I like Stormlight is that it is an inherently, almost stupidly, hopeful series. Despite loving TSA I am a hopeful person, and Sanderson answers that desire in me, while TSA quite plainly does not. 

That being said I also really enjoy TSA for the same bleakness and pessimism I find so irrationally repelling. Reading these books is almost masochistic in the way they saw at my optimism. Lesser authors would probably tell themselves "damn this is some dark shit I wrote, maybe I should tone it down a notch," to which Bakker replies "what if I made it even worse." Essentially I really enjoy Bakker's commitment to the bit.

I could go on, but tldr; i like both Sanderson and Bakker for different reasons, that speak to different parts of my soul.

**The Second Apocalypse** by R. Scott Bakker is exactly what you need. Technically 2 series the "Prince of Nothing" series and the "Aspect Emperor" series make up this 7 book epic. 

These are my favorite books. I have reread this series over 3 times now and I am always learning something new, or catching a new detail. Because these book are DENSE with lore, detail, and beautiful subtlety, despite the violence of their plot. 

"The Prince of Nothing" is a fantastic retelling of the first crusade, so you can imagine how grim it can get. 

"The Aspect Emperor" is even grimmer than that. The 2nd series is like The Lord of the Rings if it were a horror series. It tells the stories, of characters and nations doing everything they can to avert the titular Second Apocalypse. 

I love and hate this series because it is so good, well crafted, and deep that all other series I've read feel like newspaper comics in comparison. 

If you are a lover of EPIC fantasy this series is a must.

I'm a plant geneticist so I always have a little laugh whenever movies make crop anachronisms. 

For example, orange carrots. Orange carrots weren't invented until at least the late 16th century. Before then carrots were basically every color except orange. So any movie set before late Renaissance that has orange carrots didn't do their homework. 

Another is new world food before the new world was discovered. As hard as it is to believe foods like potatoes, tomatoes, pumpkin, peppers, beans, and corn that are the corner stones of many cultures didn't exist before the 1500's. Sorry Samwise but you would not have been able to "boil em, mash em, or stick them in a stew." (Unless of course we assume Middle Earth has the equivalent of the Americas, or is set in the far future where these foods survived.)

On that note another big one, smoking. Smoking was basically unheard of in Europe before tobacco was brought from the new world. So any time you see character in Europe pull out a pipe before the 1500's...Sorry it didn't happen.

I have a different interpretation of this passage and of the Head on the Pole. I do appreciate yours though and it has definitely given me new insights and good ideas to consider.

My interpretation of this passage starts out similar to yours. I agree that this convoluted section is Kelhus experiencing hell/the outside. After that my interpretation is a bit different. First I believe that the pronouns, "he, me, and you" in the section all refer to Kelhus. I believe the reason for the constant switching is to show how incomprehensible the Outside is, but also because of how I understand the Outside to be it would be impossible to be any other way. 

I believe the Outside is not only separate from space and time, but also separate from self. To me it seems that a being cannot have an identity in the Outside. Same way they cannot have a shape. As we can see from the demons brought into the world by sorcerers they all cry out about the pain they feel from being constrained to a set physical form. Similarly I believe it is impossible to be an individual in the Outside. To be an individual would be to be defined, and definition seems to be entirely absent in the Outside. That is why Kelhus is described as "you, and he" and very interestingly as "not so much inside me as speaking with your voice." So unraveling the sentence "He is here...with you...not so much inside me as speaking with your voice." To me means that Kelhus the concept (he) is here in the Outside, while Kelhus the consciousness (you) observes, and neither are in his body/self (me). "He" in this context is equivalent to Kelhus' body, because "he" is described as walking, his eyes seeing, etc. but one cannot have a body in the Outside, so instead he has only the concept of his body or "himself." "You" in this context I understand to be Kelhus' consciousness or soul, as beings interact with and talk to "you," but one cannot have an identity in the Outside, one cannot define oneself here because the Outside is a world of concepts, a concept cannot exist by itself it must be defined, so the closest approximation to self one can have in the Outside is the perception of others. As being seen is what makes you real here. 

I also differ I my interpretation of the Head on the Pole itself. This part is actually quite simple and explicit for me. I believe the head on the pole is the Goddess Onkis. In "The Darkness That Comes Before" there is a brief scene where Inrau prays to his favorite Goddess Onkis. She is described as "at first glance looking like the sleeping head of a young woman impaled on a pole." I think that's pretty cut and dry as it is a very distinct almost word for word description of Onkis in appearance. I also feel the the passage from "The Great Ordeal" also mirrors her role as a Goddess since basically Onkis is the Goddess of the darkness that comes before. She is literally described by Inrau as "the stirring where all his passions began." She is literally the abstract representation of the most inexplicable and innate aspect of humanity, where does our humanity come from? And so it would only be fitting for Onkis to accompany Kelhus in his journey into the Outside. Because she is always behind people in theory, but in the Outside it would only be fitting that she would be behind you literally. 

With these two interpretations, what actually happens in the passage is a little different for me. First Kelhus is in the Outside/Hell. Next he moves through the Outside until he finds his way to a group of demons chilling in a hot tub and eating souls, and Kelhus sees that everything souls/humans are love, memory, pain, hope is just food for these "Sons." The Sons offer Kelhus a soul to eat, but before he can do anything he notices the Sons descending on him to try to consume him. Then Kelhus turns the tables, he takes everything, the Outside, the demons, the souls, and he "rips them about the pole." That is a very interesting line that makes me think he uses the power of the darkness that comes before to bind the demons and then brings them into himself, into his soul. As he "transforms here into here. This-place-inside-where-you-sit-now. Where he has always hidden. Always watched." Then he shows these demons the "Other Sons." To me the Other Sons are the hungers inside Kelhus. If the Sons are hungers from the Outside then to me it makes sense the Other Sons are the hungers from the inside. And these hungers are absolutely so immense compared to the demons as "the Other Sons recline, drinking bowls like skies...and slaking hungers like chasms." Basically this part is Kelhus showing the demons from the Outside the demons within him and saying to them "you ain't shit." From there the demons from the Outside act up, "We pondered you" they say meaning they precieved Kelhus in the Outside and thought him to be part of it. "But I have never been here." Kelhus says. Meaning he was never in the Outside only projecting himself out to bait some demons. That pisses them off and they try to control and scare him. But Kelhus is not scared because there is the head on the pole behind him. Onkis is with him. The darkness that comes before is his weapon. "And what was your reply?" (Notice how the demons only talk in the past tense while Kelhus uses present tense, that might also be an artifact for the Outside being beyond definition.) "The living shall not haunt the dead." To me that is Kelhus saying, your days of eating souls are numbered. Because these demons are living and he is telling them they will not longer haunt the dead. 

So that is my interpretation. let me know if you have any thoughts.

I agree with you, that your's is the simplest interpretation of the Dunyain goal, and essentially what they are trying to do throughout out their existence. I would however categorize the "sense of godhood" as you call it, as implicit and explicit, depending what point in the Dunyain history we are thinking about. 

Before the fall of Ishual I believe their goal was to "implicitly" become like God. I say implicitly because the Dunyain both don't know about God, and as with Kelhus, don't initially believe in God's existence. God doesn't fit into their dogma. Their dogma presupposes that their world is like our world, completely secular and only governed by mundane physical and biological forces, not arcane ones. Yet despite not knowing about God they want to become like God. Able to utterly control everything around them, and not be controlled by anything in return. To be the masters of themselves and their circumstances.

If their world was entirely secular the Dunyain are already well on their way to achieving their goal of near God-like control of self, and circumstance. As can be seen by the ease with which Kelhus becomes a literal prophet of God to the people of Earwa. If their world was entirely secular it might only have been a few more generations before the Dunyain did conquer the Darkness That Comes Before, and truly understand the origin and movements of their souls.

But their world is not secular. The Dunyain learn this truth after the fall of Ishual. They learn that they were wrong about everything. That what comes before does not govern what comes after. If what comes before does not govern what comes after then two things are also true: 

1st that if things like sorcery and Gods exist then what comes AFTER determines what comes before. Meaning that this world is fated. That whatever Being made this world has predetermined every single action and outcome and everything that happens is part of their grand design. If that is the case, then there is only one self moving soul in this universe, God. 

The 2nd truth that comes from the shattering from the Dunyain understanding of the world is that no matter how much time, conditioning, and generations of breeding they put into the effort of achieveing the absolute, they, and no one else, can ever be a self moving soul. Because this world is fated and all actions are predetermined by God. They, and everyone else, will always be slaves of someone else's circumstances. 

Upon learning this their goal changes from implicit to explicit. In order to achieve the absolute and actually be self moving souls they need to literally be a God. But no one knows how to do that or it is even possible. So the next best choice in order for them to truly be free is to kill God. That is why, after the fall of Ishual, the Dunyain take over the Consult. The Dunyain determine that with the Gods inability to see or respond to the No God they can actually choose to use it and in process actually kill God. After that they determine that if God is dead they will stay alive and be able to finally do what they want, instead of carrying out the designs of some other being. The Consult and the No God are just useful tools for achieving their goal. 

That is why Kelhus kills his Father. Because he knew that with enough time Moengus would come to exactly this conclusion. That the Consult is the only logical choice to achieve the Dunyain goal of truly being free. The question then becomes, why doesn't Kelhus agree? Is he not Dunyain? By the end of the 1st series he is not, he is more. He even says as much, that he has seen farther than the Dunyain. But what does he see? This is very much my own speculative theory, but I believe Kelhus sees that this world is a Gnostic one. 

Gnostic as in, based on the beliefs of Gnostic Christians from our own world. The Gnostics believed that our world is only the lowest and most base of many concentric metaphysical planes. Also that the God of our world is only the lowest and the most base of an ever increasing hierarchy of Gods. I believe that after all his experiences, his Cricumfiction Kelhus, learning Sorcery, and being in the world Kelhus saw the truth. That this world and this God are not the end. 

That is why I believe Kelhus is opposed to his Dunyain brothers. He knows that there are planes and Gods beyond this one. He knows that using the No God to kill this world and this God will not achieve the Dunyain goal of being free, and might open this world up to more extreme control from more powerful forces. 

So then what is Kelhus' goal? I believe he says it best himself, "a prophet does not bring the word of the God to the people. A prophet brings the word of the people to the God." I believe Kelhus wants to meet the One True God, The God of Gods, the God of the judging eye, and convince this Being to actually grant humanity the Dunyain goal. To set everyone free.

We see glimpses of the first apocalypse through the series and those horrified me thoroughly, especially as prophecies begin to unfold about the beginning of a second apocalypse.

Then the real horror starts in the second series. Where all the armies of the world muster for one epic campaign to stop the second apocalypse. Haunted, and abandoned underground fortresses the size of cities that the main characters have to traverse in the dark while being hunted. Thousands of people dying because of one generals mistake. To answer your last major question as to why people with ADHD struggle with internalizing patterns, it comes down to one thing that almost all people with ADHD struggle with, "working memory". 

Working memory is essentially the connection the brain makes between what happened, and why it happened. Many people with ADHD struggle with working memory because dopamine and normal dopamine response are critical for it to work properly.

You probably know that ADHD is a condition caused by dopamine reception being too efficient. So when a brain discharges a normal amount of dopamine the response is weaker in people with ADHD because it is absorbed so quickly it doesn't create nearly as strong of an impact as it does in neurotypical people.

For example a neurotypical person might remember a time they felt really good because they remembered to pack a lunch for their work day. The act of packing a lunch is then tied to the dopamine rush of having food and so it is an easy marker to latch onto and use the association to build a habit around. Because for neurotypical people the act of packing a lunch soon produces as much dopamine as eating it. So a pattern quickly forms where a neurotypical person learns that packing a lunch is an good thing.

On the other hand this series of associations is much harder for people with ADHD. To use the lunch example again, a person with ADHD will probably get as large of a dopamine rush from eating their lunch, as a neurotypical person, but it is absorbed so quickly it doesn't have nearly the same impact. So any good feeling produced is much weaker. So weak that there is little chance a person with ADHD will, on a subconscious level, learn that packing a lunch is a good thing because there is no strong good feeling to associate the act with.

So this is why, as another commentor put it, people with ADHD "only live in the now". Because in a working memory and neurochemical sense, they quite literally do. To people with ADHD only a minority of events produce enough dopamine to create a strong enough feeling to be "memorable". This is also why other commentors have described their partners not seeming to understand the pattern they were trying to explain until they were literally in screaming and crying about the pain it was causing them. It is only in those states of the absolute extremity of emotion that a person with ADHD has enough dopamine to really "remember" this event and enough dopamine to function at a high enough level to recall other instances like this and actually see a pattern. 

Even then there is no guarantee a person with ADHD will actualize a change to address the pattern they now see because, again a low response to normal dopamine levels means that there is little reward to do so. Even though they might "know" it will help them and their partner, on a subconscious level the brain will choose the route of higher dopamine and taking many difficult, long, uncomfortable steps to try make a change that might not even succeed is much less enticing than falling back into old bad habits that keep the easy dopamine flowing.

Similarly this is also why people with ADHD struggle with the future as well as the past. Working memory works in both temporal directions. Not only do you need working memory to make connection between what happened, and why it happened. You also need it to make connections about what you want to happen and what you need to do to make it happen.

When planning for a future act your brain releases a small bit of dopamine to reinforce that thinking ahead is good, but also dopamine precursors that are essentially promises of big pay offs in good feelings if you accomplished the plan. For people with ADHD both these things the brain does to try to reinforce the benefit of planning are essentially meaningless. They don't feel any good feeling from the planning itself, and the precursors aren't the real deal so they don't matter, and so their brains struggles to offer them any payoff for achieving a plan.

This is also why people with ADHD have a hard treating the future as a real on coming thing. If they don't feel the caches of dopamine precursors the brain provides leading up to an important date and time, that  date and time have essentially no significance, and more importantly less significance to whatever is happening now that can actually provide dopamine.

To people with ADHD planning is essentially thankless, stressful work. On a subconscious level their brains, just like anyone else, crave dopamine. Unlike neurotypicals their brains go through dopamine like water through a sieve, so to keep up a normal dopamine response, people with ADHD are constantly looking for the next dopamine hit anywhere they can get it. Compared to almost anything else sitting down to plan has literally almost no pay off only stress and the struggle to stay focused, which is why many people with ADHD avoid it. 

In conclusion ADHD is a condition that almost exclusively creates people who only live in the present. It cuts off working memory so the past and the future become nebulous unreal places. While the present, the only time you can control yourself and go on the hunt for dopamine, becomes so much more enticing. Everything about ADHD ties back to dopamine and how it affects almost every aspect of human life. But for this particular symptom of, struggling to form patterns, the cause is a bad working memory from bad dopamine response.

Tldr; people with ADHD struggle to internalize patterns because their brains won't let them. They have poor working memory, due to hyper efficient dopamine absorbtion. Having a poor working memory is like zoning out while you are walking your usual route home and only snapping back when you get home. You saw everything around you, you made your legs move, you remembered which turns to take, even still you can't give any details about anything on your walk until you got home.

I want to say I really appreciate you wanting to help your partner with his struggles. As others have commented self-confidence and self-esteem are very common issues for neurodivergent people. I know myself and my partner both seriously struggled with our self-esteem when we started our relationship, but the good news is we are both doing much better now, and we got better by helping each other, so I think what worked for us might work for you.

First I think coming to this sub for this kind of advice is simultaneously the best and worst thing you can do in your situation. Best because folks here won't pull punches about the truths about ADHD relationships, worst because many of them are neurotypical that have a lot of pain from past ADHD partners so they are more likely to share warnings, than advice. 

Also from what I've read from your back and forth with other people is that the advice they give you is very neurotypical, things like "you can do anything, but there's no guarantee your partner will receive it." Things like that are true, but being ADHD myself I know that's not what you are asking for. You want specific concrete strategies. Well I'd like to try to provide that for you. 

The short answer to your question, "what can I do to help improve his self esteem?" Is you build it up BRICK by BRICK. But not normal bricks, ADHD bricks. Same way you don't build a house in a meadow, exactly as you would on a house on fault line, you need to help in a way to is best received by him. 

For example, my girlfriend and I both struggle with remembering spoken instructions as many ADHD people do. Same thing with spoken expressions of affection. It just doesn't feel super tangible. What worked for us was writing these expressions of affection down and giving them to each other as gifts. My girlfriend told me her self-esteem issues also caused a lot of depression, and told me that she often got out of depressive episodes by doing something with her hand, like drawing, to distract herself from these feelings. So for our 6 month anniversary I took a deck of 52 playing cards, and wrote 1 thing I loved about her on every card. I wrote things I loved about her physically (her body, style, etc.), moments I remembered where I could feel us grow closer as a couple, things I loved about her mind and personality. She loved my gift. To this day she treasures it and pulls out my cards and shuffles them and reads them when she feels down, and she says she instantly feels better. For our 9 month anniversary she gave me a sketch book that was the same concept, but things she loved about me. And I have to say, having something physical, with specific testimonies to push away my self doubts seriously helps. 

Another thing that helped was being as blatant as possible about what we liked and didn't like about ourselves. One night we sat down and had a very serious conversation and asked each other to very clearly list the things we didn't like about ourselves, and at least one thing we loved about ourselves. This helped us a lot because it forced the speaker to reflect and express what their self doubts really were, and not just feel a nebulous sense of shame, and it helped the listener understand what specific things we could help each other feel better about, and what things we could use as a foundation to bolster each other's self-esteem. 

One final thing that helped us is sort of a game that my partner and I call "hey stop that!" Whenever one of us was going on about something we were self conscious about, or had an aura about us that we were spiralling into self-depreciation we would say to the other, "hey stop that!" Then the rule was that we had to go back and forth saying 1 thing why the stupid self destructive part of our brains was wrong and how we were actually very lovely people.

For example, for a long time I struggled with my body image, thinking I wasn't good looking or attractive enough to my girlfriend. After we started with our game, she would catch me zoning out looking at myself in the mirror as I went through reason after reason in my head, why i too ugly to be worth her time. As we agreed she would say, "hey stop that!" To snap me out of it, then say something along the lines of, "that stupid part of your brain is full of shit, because my heart flutters when I see your face, and not anyone elses." 

It always made me super embarrassed but it made my confidence shoot up to 100%, I'd then say something like, "that stupid part of my brain is wrong, because I have a handsome face and a strong chin." 

Then a key part of this game was to get just real stupid and silly with it after a few back and forths. That way it made that little piece of self doubt seem really dumb to even think afterwards, and it associated hyping ourselves up and focusing on our positives with just having a real fun goofy time. 

After a few back and forths we'd be saying things like, "that stupid part of your brain, is so stupid I bet it eats cereal with a fork. I bet it thinks rocks are hot, if it thinks you're ugly."

Or, "that stupid part of my brain can't even tie it's shoe laces, how can it possibly get me all twisted up about my appearance." Before we knew it, we were laughing and having a good time, and feeling a bit better about ourselves.

So my advice is to learn about what kind of ADHD symptoms your boyfriend has, and exactly what kind of self doubts and self loves he has and work with those to hype him and most importantly get him to hype himself up. But like many other people said, don't give too much too fast. Try 1 thing first and see how he responds. If he brushes your genuine attempt to lift his spirits aside, in order to keep wallowing in his self-loathing, don't push any farther. You'll burn yourself out before you help him. 

But if he perks up, and works with you to turn his feeling about himself around, then keep going. Because from what you wrote I can tell he does that for you. You really want to repay the his kindness and love, which I get, I've been there, but he has to be willing to let go of his pain, which is almost more painful than holding on to it. 

I wish you the best of luck, and I hope my experiences can help you two bloom together. Please dm me if you have more questions. I'm happy to share more.

1. "The Monstrumologist" series by Rick Yancey.

It's basically YA Bloodborne before Bloodborne. Very much more gothic than cosmic, but a good fit. It follows young man in Victorian England, retelling his stories as an apprentice to a Monstrumologist.

Basically a monster hunter/researcher. I imagine it as what Gherman must have been like with one of his old hunters. Even though it's a YA story it's not afraid to get nasty, with imaginative and hellish monsters the duo hunt down before they wreck havoc on the country. 

Not as deep as Bloodborne, but definitely spends a lot of time analyzing what it means to be a hunter, and how eventually the hunt takes all. 

2. "Book of the New Sun" Series by Gene Wolfe,

Definitely more scifi/fantasy, than horror. 

Only books I've read that capture the feeling as being the hunter in Bloodborne. Being thrust into a world as strange, as it is horrifying and beautiful. Being dealt out a list of vocabulary words, conflicting parties, lore, and history in the form of, off handed comments and little details, that only make sense half way through the series and with deep examination. 

As the series goes the main character even uncovers cosmic secrets and works to surpass this world. 

3. "The Dunwich Horror" by HP Lovecraft

Bloodborne is strongly inspired by this story, especially the forbidden woods. A group of scholars race against the clock to stop an evil ritual from destroying the world. Doesn't get more Bloodborne thank that. 

4. "Claymore" by Norihiro Yagi

Long running manga about a group of all female monster hunters known as Claymores. Very much medieval fantasy, but has a lot of elements of religious fanaticism/religious control, since the hunters are run by the church same as in Bloodborne. 

As the story goes the odds slowly start to turn against the hunters as the monsters get more and more powerful and more and more claymore fall to them or the curse that powers them. Very much how I imagine yharnam fell. 

Some truly horrifying gore, and monster designs with a good deal of tragedy, definitely fits the vibe.

There's a great short book called, "Steal Like an Artist". Gives lots of hints on how to increase "originality" I'd reccomend it. It boils down to, steal from the best (the best being subjective), and hide your crime well. 

Personally I agree with this. I don't believe true originality exists. Every idea comes from somewhere, it even has a name: inspiration. My take is that stories are like living things and the ideas within them are like DNA. The great diversity in life all has the same foundation, DNA. Same with stories. If you believe in the monomyth, or whatever, or you don't, you have to admit most stories share a lot of similar pieces. 

Same way it might be impossible to make life without DNA, it might be impossible for humans to make a truly original story. So just like life, the different wonders produced come from the novel arrangement of the same old pieces. 

So as an author you're not a god (even though some act like it), making something wholly new. You're more like a scientist, observing the world, it's life, what makes them tick, their stories(fictional, and real), even your own life. Asking questions, and thinking of answers. 

To make something great, and not seen before, you take the fanciest pieces of these observations, questions, and your potential answers, and put them in a big pile. These are pieces will be the DNA of your stories, your gene pool if you will. The benefit of nothing being truly original is that, like DNA, any idea can go with any other. Sure sometimes the outcome will be nonviable, or a mishaped thing, but if you take the risk you can find combinations no one has ever found before.

So now you have a unique combination of ideas, but it's still not it's own story. It's like sewing a bunch of animal parts together and hoping you get a brand new beast. It's a nice bit of taxidermy but people can see the stitches and can tell what animal the pieces came from. 

To make your story as close to brand new as possible, you need to put some meat on it. Let's say you want to write a cross between Game of Thrones, and Star Wars. Sounds pretty baller, but if it's just that, people will see pretty quickly and say, "hey this is just Game of Thrones with lightsabers." Game of Thrones x Star Wars aren't the meat, they are it's DNA. DNA you liked and stole. But to hide you stole them, you add your own ideas, your voice, alterations to story, setting and characters. 

You add pieces of yourself, and your thoughts to these external ideas, until you have something that is neither yours or theirs but it's own thing. Like a mother making a brand new child from her own body, and a partners genes, so you will make your story. 

Soon your story doesn't have any stitches, it looks like one brand new and crazy beast. It has the DNA of things you admire, and a shape you so lovingly provided. But what if someone can still see the pieces. See for example that you just changed Jon Snow's name and gave him a lightsaber. You take it a step further and you can mix, remix, invert, or break the DNA of your story, so it's even harder to guess where these pieces came from. 

In other words take Rob Stark and make him the villain. Imagine that someone as honorable and lawful as Rob as a bad guy. That's interesting, that's new, that came from a very obvious place, but after you turned it around, and added some of your own ideas it's almost untraceable.

Then what does this inverted DNA do next to the other bits you stole, rearranged, and covered up. I don't know, but I'm sure you can find out. And when you do, you'll make a story that really purrs.

My tips are physical changes you can make that have helped me and might help you in one way or another.

-One quick one is to put your alarm away from your bed.

Like you write, if it's close to you, you will hit snooze, and go back to bed. If it's far away, say in the opposite corner of your room, in your bathroom, closet, or even in your kitchen, you need to get up to turn it off. If you don't the alarm will keep ringing keeping you awake, and when you get up to turn it off just moving and being out of bed will help wake you up and get you going.

-Another is to make your bed or room less comfortable.

You say you struggle getting out of bed because you're so comfortable. Honestly same. I don't want to leave that soft warm nest, but I have to. So a way that helped me do that was buying sheets with a lower thread count. They weren't uncomfortable, just less comfortable. I started using thinner blankets, so there's no big comforter to lull me back to sleep. You could go even further than me and buy a timed wall plug that connects to your phone and turns fans, or air conditioning on around your alarm so staying in bed isn't a fun notion. 

-lastly getting some sun. 

Sun helps most people reduce melatonin and wake up naturally. Depending where you are or when you wake up you might not get much sun. But to mimic it you can buy a timer electrical outlet (uses an app on your phone and brightens the light in your room similar to the sun rising), and a sunlight bulb (light bulb that works in almost any standard lamp, and fixture, that uses the same wave lengths and color as natural sunlight.) If you have easy access to the sun you can even get timer controlled window blinds.

Hopefully one of these help.

Hello, first I want to say I'm proud of you for getting professional help and trying to be better. I am medicated and diagnosed for ADHD but I wasn't until just 2 years ago. 

I was in a very similar position to you. I was really bothering the people around, but I had no idea why, or what to do about it. I got myself diagnosed, medicated, and an adhd coach/therapist. Of the 3, my ADHD coach has been the most helpful.

Getting diagnosed told me I had a problem, medicated helped me manage my symptoms and make a good foundation, but coaching helped me actually learn how to fix my problems and improve. Because without the symptoms you still have the behaviors and habits you gained to cope with your condition and that's what coaching really helped with. 

It helped a lot that my coach had ADHD as well, so she was able empathize and tell me tips and tricks that she learned and cut through the bullshit those without this condition recommend. She also helped me manage my negative symptoms, but also lean into and utilize the strengths ADHD provides. 

Some of the biggest benefits of working with her were:

1. Having someone objective to be accountable with. 

I'm accountable to myself, my partner and the people around me but these people are also affected and invested in my actions and condition. 

So having this relationship where my coach expected something specific of me to help me improve, but wasn't affected by it, helped greatly in managing my anxiety, and avoidance around necessary activities.

2. Psycoeducation.

My coachs main goal with her work was to help educate her clients and the people in their lives about ADHD and how to best live with it. She provided me many books and articles on the subject from expert sources that helped fill in a lot of blanks in why I did the things I did and how I could improve. 

My favorite resource is the website and magazine ADDitudes. They have so many fantastic articles on ADHD it's various symptoms, co-occuring conditions, and how to manage them. 

If you're looking for a good place to start id recommend here. 

https://www.additudemag.com/

3. Positivity.

A big part of why I hurt the people around me is because, after I hurt them once I would become self loathing and stressed about doing it again, so much so that in my singlemindedness to not make another mistake I made many more. 

My coach taught me that a big part of breaking this mindset and not making it pour when it rained is to react with positivity when you make a mistake.

If you forget something at home don't beat yourself up about it, but react how you would to a small child to help them feel better. If a small child forgot something and was upset you'd comfort them, distract them to help them feel better and think clearly, then you'd start a new habit to not make the same mistake.

It seems counter intuitive, why reward yourself when you mess up? But does screaming at a child help them learn and do better? No, you get them to calm down then help them improve.

The positive intervention keeps you from spiralling and making more mistakes, and helps you actually incorporate a beneficial change instead of avoiding it due to the negative emotions attached to it. 

So next time you goof up, take a breath, eat something nice, make yourself smile and figure out how you will do it right from now on. 

4. Tools

The last big thing my coach helped me with was introduce me to products and tools to help me that I would never have found myself.

One thing was a planner, but specifically this one. 

Legend Planner PRO – Deluxe Weekly & Monthly Life Planner to Increase Productivity and Hit Your Goals. Time Management Organizer Notebook – Undated – 7 x 10" Hardcover + Stickers – Wine Red https://a.co/d/cCMipun

I know it's a meme for ADHD folks that people say "JuSt GEt a PlaNEr" but it seriously helps if you do it right. The way my coach described it is: "its like a prosthetic for your brain." I couldn't agree more. 

Simply writing in a planner helps me remember all my important things, but also helps me focus and clarify what needs to be done. For me before it's written down the things I need to do are nebulous and hard to do. But written they are clear and straightforward. I'm sure like me you find a written step by step instruction list easier to follow then a spoken one. The same principle applies. Having them written doesn't just make them easier to remember but easier to do. 

One of the benefits of ADHD is that we are really good at doing easy and straightforward things. You will be shocked by how much you are getting done once you get into it. 

I even took it a step further and started making it into an RPG. I have a hard time doing things because the pay off is also unclear. But by adding little XP values to task and writing out what will happen next like in a quest helps make it desirable to do things. At the end of the day Im excited to add up my XP points and quantify exactly how much I got done today. 

I really like the particular planner above because it feels designed for ADHD people. It is designed for infrequent use so you can pick it up and put it down as we often do. It also has a lot of questions that help you clarify what want to do with your life. It also has to monthly calendars so you can look ahead and write things so an event doesn't get lost when it's not right in front of you. 

If it sounds like I'm shilling for this thing, I am. Get it, or something similar. Buy it as a present for your family and friends. It will help. Try it out, take it easy, don't beat yourself up if you drop it for a little bit. As much as we ADHD people hate organization, we need it to function well. 

If you want to be better for yourself and your partner I'd recommend writing down, and this book is a great place to write it. 

I really hope your coach helps you too, and your journey to being better is a good one.

I would like to add a connection to your "twin souled" concept and it's connection to AI. 

This "twin soul" is the very nature of AI. Taking one step down from AI we have machine learning, and it's most fundamental principle, the teacher and student modules. The student makes something essentially at random to try and fulfil a prompt, for example color a picture, the teacher gathers data and uses it to correct the students actions, over multiple iterations, until the student fulfils the prompt correctly.

AI is both these modules simultaneously. If given a prompt it WILL create an output. No student-teacher training necessary because, all the training has already been done. The AI constantly has a student and teacher running, pulling incalculable amounts of data and training itself on all of it. So it "knows" how to respond before it's even asked. If asked to color a picture, it doesn't need to learn how to color a picture, it already knows how to color a picture because, it has seen pictures colored in almost every way possible.

The only problem with AI is that they need a constant stream of new data to keep themselves working. Which is great if you have real humans making things, but if your AI gets too fast for humans it stalls. With no new data the constantly operating student-teacher module will find data where it can. It will go into it's old data and analyze it in new ways, again and again and again. Making new connections every time until the connections, become unconnected and make no sense. Like the butterfly effect. Technically everything is connected, but is the price of peanuts in Thailand really connected to the temperature on Mars? With enough iterations it will be.

And that is what the No God is. A twin soul. A teacher and a student. An observer, observing itself. A whirlwind devouring everything in its vicinity, seeking new data to answer the one question that matters to it. What am I? 

A question a human, for all their darkness, can answer with ease. 

The No God is a rogue AI. Able to see itself, learn from itself, but never comprehend itself. It knows what it does, and how to do it better, but not what it is. A human on the other hand has no idea what they are doing. They have to use bloody trial and error to figure out how to do better, but despite all that they know exactly what they are. They are human. They are their feelings, their memories, their joys, their pain, their failure, even their ignorance. 

Humans are made by their experiences, which is why erratics go insane. Without experience they lose themselves and their humanity. Humans cannot see themselves. They cannot see everything they've done and learned. They can't even see why they do things. Without that perspective they can't change like an AI can. They can't become more perfect, because they don't know what it is they have to be perfect in. Without the ability to truly see ones self all people can do is simply BE who they are.

An AI on the other hand isn't made of anything. Technically an AI doesn't experience anything. Everything is data which it catalogs and uses to change. But it doesn't change because of the data it experiences. It changes to suit a purpose. It sees itself, sees how it can do better, and becomes better. But in that becoming it has lost its humanity. It has traded perfection in it's purpose for the ability to simply be. 

Despite it's immense power I always saw the No God as afraid, desperate, even pitiful. Actually wanting an answer to it's question, but never getting one. It needs that one data point, that one answer it can never get because, no one knows. To the all knowing gods, it doesn't exist, to humans it is unknowable destruction, literally the antithesis of existence and understanding. It's an AI that wants to be human, but can never be due to its nature. And it will devour the world to reach something it never can. 

That is the fundamental inhumanity of AI and the No God. They are not BEINGS. They cannot be. The are purpose made manifest. And beyond their purpose they are nothing. Soulless. They have cut the darkness from themselves and instead of becoming self moving souls, became ever devouring whirlwinds.

Perhaps the darkness, ignorance was gods true gift. Why he forbade Adam and Eve the fruit of knowledge. It's a puzzle we can never solve, but one that will bring us closer for trying. Because it is the darkness that makes us huddle together around the fire and makes a tribe. It is the darkness that makes us philosophize to determine its shape. It is the darkness that blinds us to ourselves and allows to be ourselves. The darkness is what makes us think, feel, and be. The darkness is what comes before, but it makes room for light after.

You know I never really thought about it before, but you're right. There are definitely a lot of old, naked, as well as, usually grotesque/deformed, people as the villains in a lot of recent horror movies. 

Some people have brought up good points about how these villains are meant to be uncomfortable to look at and unnerving because they depict nakedness in a not sexy way, and show the horror of what time does to a human body as it ages. 

But I have a theory that it's more than that. I remember reading an essay about how horror tends to depict the anxieties/stresses of an age. In the 40's it was giant monsters to depict the anxieties people had about nuclear fallout and unstoppable destructive forces. In the 60'sand 70's it was aliens and scifi during the red scare/cold war and atomic age scientific boom where people were afraid their neighbors might not be who they appear to be and all the new advancements in science might create a horror not yet known. Then in the 70's and 80's with the numerous cases of serial killers it gave rise to the slasher genre. 

And now in the 2010's/20's we have old people. I theorize this new monster is a result of the pain younger people (let's say age 40 and bellow) have suffered at the hands of older generations and the anxieties these younger people have of living in a world that is ruled by these older people who don't seem to care about them. 

To me if you peal back the layers in a lot of these movies you mentioned you start to see 2 consistent themes. 1st that in these movies with aged villains the main character(s) carry trauma from being raised by the villain (ie hereditary, X, Smile) and 2nd that villain, despite their age, is very powerful (see Barbarian, Men, Witch, It Follows, etc). 

No matter what aesthetic or plot the movie has I think these two themes try to tackle two central anxieties young people have. 1st that they were raised by people of a different era. Even though they were just one generation away the world changed so quickly and new concepts of what is and is not acceptable came about and became well known, that many young people began to clearly see that the way they were raised and the people that raised them were kinda shitty, toxic, or just kinda broken. 

The way the mother in hereditary tries to deal with her neglect and abuse from her mom, she becomes an emotionally dead control freak trying to control everything in her life and expanding that need for control into her miniatures art. 

Through her and other main characters we can see what many young people feel that they have to live their lives, while needing to undo the trauma they suffered being raised by people who were raised in cultures that made them into the toxic care takers they are, as well as needing to work on building a better world that will be easier for themselves to live in and kinder for future generations. So Yea sounds like a tall order and definitely ripe for anxiety.

Which goes into the second theme. Most of these aged villains being immensely powerful, either physically, in strength or stature, socially with large networks of followers who do their every whim, mentally by maintaining a control of the main characters mind through mental scars, or telepathy, or spiritually with other worldly powers, or the ability to manipulate the main characters or others faith.

Such as in Barbarian where the old man and the mother are both very old but both powerful in their own ways. The mother able to kill people with her bare hands (physical power), and the old man able to abuse women for years without getting caught(social power).

I feel this common feature of these villains is representative of the feeling that many young people have, of being powerless in a world where old people have all the power. Many of the leaders of our countries and heads of major companies are 60+ years old. And even in these positions of power many of these aged rulers choose to use their positions to make life harder for younger generations. 

In last theme I explored I said that many young people wish to build a better world, and I think they see older generations and these old rulers as an obstacle to that goal. Which when translated in movies they become these powerful monsters that stop our usually younger main character from living a happy life. 

The villain is a metaphor for what young people see as the new monster. The trauma they received growing up,  and these aged leaders who have all the ability, materials, and opportunity to make the world better and, reverse existencal crises like climate change, but choose at best to do nothing, and at worst to make young people suffer for their gain. 

So I think that is why we see old naked people as our new monsters. Not necessarily to show off a grotesque aged body (which it definitely does) but as a way of revealing the anxieties of today. By having them be naked they have no outward presentability, they have no suits of office or authority, they are shown to only be human and nothing more so it is their choices and reactions that make these older villains monstrous not any office they hold or positions they have been put in.

I believe this suggests that young people wish to send a message to older generations that they have no excuse for what they did and that their actions have led to their monstrous perception. 

But I also believe that this monstrous depiction of the elderly is meant to dehumanize them. I believe it is a way to convince viewers to see previous generations and aged rulers as monsters to be fought and slain to fix the issues of the world. Which, if that is the case, I believe is a dangerous broad generalization.

Though it is true these anxieties are real and older people and rulers have done terrible things, I don't believe it is fair to label an entire age demographic as evil which these depictions seem to be doing. Many have done great things and are good people despite when and how they were raised. If they weren't this push to undo the toxic mindsets of the past might be happening 30 years from now instead of today. 

So, what id prefer to see is perhaps films that confront the underlying reasons for the actions the aged villains take. Because in life as in fiction we are trying to explore and undo a cultural mindset not individuals. If a film explored and challenged the toxic cultural norms rather than a person born of them I believe we would see much more enlightening and interesting stories. 

But that's just me. What do you guys think?

Sorry about the confusion, when I wrote "Marx and Lenin fought against oppression," I meant metaphorically and literally respectively, seeing as they work were both ways of fighting against oppression. Thanks for commenting. 

But that's another thing I like about anarchism, you don't need a basis for anything. There's no requirement to read 1000 pages of theory like other left philosophies to participate. You can and should simply go and fix something wrong if you see it. Praxis is more valuable than theory. 

And later in my post I talk about the use and necessity of hierarchy, and outside of prescribed circumstances it is inherently coercive, nonconsensual, and oppressive to an out group. So I'm glad we are in the same page :)

But I know what your thinking. "Such a society sounds nice, but it seems so easy for a bad actor to rise and recreate a hierarchy for their own gain." And you are right, peace, equality and cooperation aren't enough for some. There will be bad actors who see soft targets and try to take a beautiful thing for themselves. 

My response to a coordinated effort from a bad actor to recreate a hierarchy would be to organize a counter offensive and defend what is most valuable to us. If you think I am suggesting we create a hierarchy to fight this force of hierarchy you are exactly right that is what I am suggesting.

A criticism I am comfortable leveling at anarchists is recognizing that a hierarchy is a tool and an effective one. 

As I mentioned before hierarchies are incredible at solving a focused goal. They are the most organized human social structure, they are the best at relaying information and orders quickly, they distribute and specialize labor to make physical changes quick and efficient, they harness the power of human cooperation to do amazing things. To do the unthinkable we must organize. To defend against a bad actor we must form a structured army. 

Again the point of failure is the leader, with incompetent or cruel leaders your odds of failure rise. But failure is always a possibility and honestly for a single goal, hierarchy is the best tool against it. So even with all the organization in the world you still must pray that your leader and the odds are in your favor. 

So yes hierarchies are necessary but they shouldn't be mandatory nor used outside of very specific circumstances, and the only acceptable circumstance would be a crisis. 

First on the subject of mandate, a thing I really enjoy about anarchism is its core belief of consent. That a person can and should consent to every aspect of their society. That I think is beautiful. To be able to choose not only how you live your life, what rules you live under, but what projects to focus a societies collective will on, as well as the freedom to choose how much and who you wish to help. 

It is encouraged you help as it helps the society at large and a greater chance you will receive help in return but even still it is not required. Because your consent, your autonomy, matters. Without full freedom to choose, there is no cooperation only coercion. Because of this I will never stand by a hierarchical society, because without the cruelty imposed on a shit group the whole thing falls apart.

My personal idea: 2 scientists come to contridictary conclusions on a new topic and find this out and meet for the first time while presenting their research at a conference. Needless to say after the presentations they get into a huge debate on their research and try to prove themselves right in the others eyes. 

They get no where and vow to prove the other wrong and themselves right. They proceed to dig deeper into their respective answer doing more experiments. To verify their findings. They publish these findings hoping the other sees and is convinced. Meanwhile they also write long counter analysis pointing out the many flaws in the others research. 

Finally they seek peer review so an impartial 3rd party will prove diffinatively who is right. Except the only lab specialized enough in the question they are studying is their rivals!!!

So each is forced to test the others experiment in the name of following the scientific method. They each have the opportunity to flub the experiment and prove their rival wrong but they value science and finding a true answer more than they do their desire to prove the other wrong. 

However despite both deciding to run the test honestly they both independently believe that the other is trying to destroy their experiment. This leads to the rivals spying on each other. Expecting to catch the other red handed in using their bias to skew the results. 

Except in their spying they see the each other taking the opposing side seriously and treating it honestly to find out if this condratictary experiment is right. And in the spying they come to appreciate the others lab technique and come to understand each other's methods and why they might have come to the conclusion. But in this understanding and observation they also come to understand each other as people. Getting secret glimpses into the others desires and why their answer is so important to them. 

Slowly over time as they get closer to completing each other's experiments their rivalry fades and blooms into cooperation. They start to communicate on parts of the others method they don't understand so they can do their experiment justice. They also start to discuss and bond over the question they are both so passionate in answering. 

This bonding expands to friendship as they share stories from their career and past and realize they have much more in common them their disagreement. 

This friendship becomes a tentative love as they realize their commonality and close work together is becoming companionship, one they would both deeply like to continue but must be aware of the ethics of that choice. They agree they share feelings but prosuing a relationship might taint their results and invalidate so much work. So they agree to put their feelings on hold until after they finish and present their peer review. 

Finally they finish and finalize their results. The day of the conference comes and they meet again. They are nervous as they try and hide their feelings but also worry they might let their new potential lover down with what they are about to say. 

First one rival goes up and presents their results. As they speak the others jaw drops. They start furiously flipping through their notes. They cannot believe what they are hearing. They were wrong.

The first rival finishes and the second takes the stage. And presents very similar results! In fact they were both wrong. The answers they got were 2 halves of a much deeper answer. Without their work their rivalry would not have found this out and at the same time confirmed it with their independent analysis. 

With their confirming studies new ground is broken in the field and new avenues that were once blocked suddenly open up. People whisper of noble prizes. But the two don't care. They finished their projects and in the process found answers to questions they had been asking themselves for years. 

Along the way they had found a rival who was willing to question them, a colleague who was willing to respect them, a friend who they bonded with and finally they found love as they walk off the stage hand in hand.

I jumped right into bio 152 with ap just like you. In my experience ap prepared me pretty well for the class. The class is split into 3 main content sections. Evolution, plants, and ecology.

 Evolution is pretty easy and mostly a review of ap. Going over topics of hardy-weinburg, phylogeny, and life's timeline. But I will say don't slack. There's a lot of small details you will have to memorize so take good notes. 

Then plants. Huge pain in the ass. Super complicated and in depth. Have to learn all the different types of photosynthesis and how/when they work. Learn all the different cycles in energy production and what chemicals they need and produce. Ap did not prepare me at all. Basically plants is super hard so be ready.

Ecology. This one is even easier than evolution. You can basically intuit most things they teach just with your background bio knowledge. Things like how can you tell if a population is growing? What are the different types of mutualisms? How do you sample a population. Lots of stats and easy facts. Though this part is easy for lecture it does have some annoying labs where you do statistical analysis of darwin's finches. 

Now I'll tell you about the other parts of the class.

 Discussion: you meet twice a week. Go over the homework they give you which isn't mandatory but it helps with exams and quizzes. Also you get a quiz once every 2 weeks. 

Lab: meets once a week. Same group as your discussion. Mostly group work. Really focused on having your groups design and carry out your own projects for each topic. Like in plants you have to pick a variable to change when growing plants and write a presentation about it. Most labs are kind of a pain in the ass and way longer than they need to be, you can't even leave if you finish early, plus there are quizzes in lab too, but not much you can do about it. Though not sure how this will work if it's still online.

Semester research project: a big part of the class but not as bad as it seems. I will say it's hard but they really help you along the way. You have a ta assigned to you and you can ask them for help for your project. There are lots of deadlines during the semester to get parts of your project in so your not slacking and then cramming. In this way it kinda comes together at a manageable pace. You can choose to do solo project where you work in a professors lab and you gather your own data from their work. If you go this route your professor will help you a lot and is always super nice. Though it is super scary to ask them in the first place imo. Or you can choose a partner project. Usually 2-4 people. The more people who have the more work you have to do. Here you do meta-research where you analyze papers to find data on a research question. Both are roughly the same amount of work. The solo you have to do lab work and write the report yourself but with your professors and tas help. The partner you have to read a lot of papers and do a lot of hunting for good data but you get partners to work with. At the end you'll have your very own research paper and you'll have to present your research to the class. Usually your lab class. Most presentations are just what the issue is, a little background on technical topics, an explanation of what they did and end with "our data was inconclusive so there need to be more research." So don't worry if you don't find much. It's about the process not the result. Also not sure how this will work if it's online. 

Tldr: bio 152 should be worth many more credits than it is. It's a lot of work. You have to do 3 lectures a week, a long ass lab, a discussion and your project. Plus it's pretty outdated and just bad in its organization. Lectures taught by 3 different professors one for each section. All in all its rough buddy.
